title: spark_read_jdbc() on databricks_connect fails with [NOT_LIST_OF_COLUMN_OR_STR] (Spark 3.4+ / 4.x)
description:
## Summary

`spark_connect(method = "databricks_connect")` succeeds, but `sparklyr::spark_read_jdbc()` then fails with:

```
pyspark.errors.exceptions.base.PySparkTypeError: [NOT_LIST_OF_COLUMN_OR_STR]
Argument `columns` should be a list[Column].
```

The same JDBC call works in a Databricks **notebook** (`method = "databricks"`, JVM Spark). This looks like a missing `pyspark_connection` implementation for JDBC, not a cluster or SQL Server problem.

Related (filed on sparklyr and closed as “not supported in pysparklyr”):

- https://github.com/sparklyr/sparklyr/issues/3461
- https://github.com/sparklyr/sparklyr/issues/3465
- https://github.com/sparklyr/sparklyr/pull/3466 (unmerged)

## Environment

- R 4.x
- sparklyr 1.9.5
- pysparklyr 0.2.2
- Databricks Connect / DBR Spark 4.x (also reproduced conceptually on Spark Connect 3.5)
- `method = "databricks_connect"`
- SQL Server via Microsoft JDBC (`com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver`)

## Minimal example

```r
library(sparklyr)
library(dplyr)

sc <- spark_connect(
  cluster_id = Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_CLUSTER_ID"),
  method     = "databricks_connect"
)

spark_query <- function(query, name = "temp") {
  tbl_name <- paste0("tbl_", name, "_", sample(10000:99999, 1))
  spark_read_jdbc(
    sc,
    name = tbl_name,
    options = list(
      url      = Sys.getenv("MSSQL_JDBC_URL"),
      user     = Sys.getenv("MSSQL_USER"),
      password = Sys.getenv("MSSQL_PASSWORD"),
      driver   = "com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver",
      dbtable  = paste0("(", query, ") AS t")
    ),
    memory = FALSE
  )
}

spark_query("SELECT 1 AS ping") %>% collect()
```

`sc` is created successfully. The error happens inside `spark_read_jdbc()`.

## What we think happens

`spark_read_jdbc()` lives in sparklyr (JVM path). pysparklyr implements `spark_read_csv` / parquet / json for Connect, but **not** JDBC, so the JVM implementation runs:

1. `overwrite = TRUE` (default) → `spark_remove_table_if_exists()` → `src_tbls()`
2. `sdf_read_column()` → `invoke(sdf, "select", column, list())`
3. PySpark Connect `DataFrame.select()` rejects the extra empty `list()` (`[NOT_LIST_OF_COLUMN_OR_STR]`)

`overwrite = FALSE` still hits `dbListTables()` in `spark_partition_register_df()`, same failure.

There is `sdf_read_column.spark_pyjobj` in pysparklyr, but Connect objects are class `spark_pyobj`, so that S3 method does not dispatch.

## Expected

```r
spark_read_jdbc(sc, name = "...", options = list(url, dbtable, user, password, driver))
```

should work on `pyspark_connection` the same way `spark_read_csv()` does: use `DataFrameReader.format("jdbc")`, and **not** call `src_tbls()` / `select(col, list())`.

`spark_write_jdbc()` has the same gap (Connect writer `save()` must not pass a filesystem path).

## Workaround (works today)

```r
opts <- list(
  url = jdbc.url, user = jdbc.user, password = jdbc.password,
  driver = "com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver",
  dbtable = paste0("(", query, ") AS t")
)
sess <- pysparklyr:::python_conn(sc)
reader <- pysparklyr:::py_invoke_options(sess$read$format("jdbc"), opts)
sdf <- reader$load()
sdf$createOrReplaceTempView(tbl_name)
dplyr::tbl(sc, tbl_name)
```

Happy to turn this into a PR (`spark_read_jdbc.pyspark_connection` / `spark_write_jdbc.tbl_pyspark`) if that helps.

title: `spark_apply(group_by =)` fails on rpy2 3.6.x: `udf-apply.py` calls the removed `pandas2ri.activate()`
description:
`spark_apply()` with a `group_by` argument fails against a Databricks Connect backend when the
worker Python has rpy2 3.6.x. Every `spark_apply()` call *without* `group_by` works on the same
cluster and the same session, so the fault is specific to one of the three UDF templates.

The template calls `pandas2ri.activate()`, which rpy2 raises from as of 3.6.0. The call also looks
redundant: the next line establishes the same conversion with `localconverter(...)`, and the two
sibling templates already use only that form.

### Reproducible example

Any grouped `spark_apply()` against a `databricks_connect` connection reaches it:

```r
library(sparklyr)
library(pysparklyr)

sc <- spark_connect(method = "databricks_connect", cluster_id = Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_CLUSTER_ID"))

tbl <- sdf_len(sc, 100) |>
  dplyr::mutate(grp = id %% 4)

# works: distributes across workers
spark_apply(tbl, function(df) data.frame(n = nrow(df)), columns = c(n = "integer"))

# fails
spark_apply(tbl, function(df) data.frame(n = nrow(df)), group_by = "grp", columns = c(n = "integer"))
```

```
pyspark.errors.exceptions.connect.PythonException:
[PYTHON_EXCEPTION] An exception was thrown from the Python worker: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 7, in r_apply
  File "/databricks/python/lib/python3.12/site-packages/rpy2/robjects/pandas2ri.py", line 378, in activate
    raise DeprecationWarning(_DEPRECATION_MSG)
DeprecationWarning:
The activate and deactivate are deprecated. To set a conversion
context check the docstring for rpy2.robjects.conversion.Converter.context.
 SQLSTATE: 38000
```

### Mechanism

`sa_function_to_string()` picks the template by whether `group_by` was supplied:

```r
udf_fn <- ifelse(is.null(.group_by), "map", "apply")
```

so `udf-apply.py` is reached only on the grouped path. That template, unchanged on `main` as of
today:

```python
def r_apply(pdf: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
  pandas2ri.activate()                                                   # <- raises on rpy2 >= 3.6.0
  r_func =robjects.r('''function(...) 1''')
  with localconverter(robjects.default_converter + pandas2ri.converter): # <- already sufficient
          ret = r_func(pdf)
          return robjects.conversion.rpy2py(ret)
```

`udf-map.py` and `udf-apply-context.py` both use only the `localconverter` form, with no
`activate()` call.

That difference looks like an oversight rather than a decision, because all three templates were
migrated in one commit: [`f0c9108`](https://github.com/mlverse/pysparklyr/commit/f0c9108),
"Addresses rpy2 deprecation warnings, and issue with context" (2025-12-04). In `udf-map.py` and
`udf-apply-context.py` that commit **deleted** the `pandas2ri.activate()` line while adding the
`localconverter` block. In `udf-apply.py` it added the block but left the `activate()` call above it.

So the two siblings have run without `activate()` since that commit, which is some evidence that
removing it here is safe. `f0c9108` is included in `v0.2.2`.

### The rpy2 boundary

The change is at 3.6.0 rather than somewhere within 3.6.x. In rpy2 3.5.17, `pandas2ri.activate()`
calls `warnings.warn(...)`; in 3.6.0 the entire body is `raise DeprecationWarning(_DEPRECATION_MSG)`.
Read from the PyPI sdists. Note that `pandas2ri` moved into the separate `rpy2-robjects`
distribution at 3.6.0.

So any environment on rpy2 3.6.0 or later cannot use `spark_apply(group_by =)`, and Databricks
runtimes ship a recent rpy2 by default: DBR 18.1's worker Python has 3.6.7.

### Suggested fix

Delete line 7 of `inst/udf/udf-apply.py`, completing what `f0c9108` did to the other two templates.
I have not patched and re-run it, so please treat that as a reading of the source rather than a
tested fix.

### Environment

- `pysparklyr` 0.2.2, `sparklyr` 1.9.5, R 4.5.2 on Posit Workbench
- Databricks Connect backend, two-worker Dedicated (`SINGLE_USER`) cluster, DBR 18.1, R 4.5.1
- rpy2 3.6.7 on both the cluster's worker Python and the client virtualenv

Observed on one workspace, one cluster, one day. I have not tested a non-Databricks `sparklyr`
backend, so I can't say whether other connection paths reach the same template.

title: `invoke` dispatch incompatibility with sparklyr 1.9.5
description:
reprex:

```r
devtools::load_all()
library(sparklyr)
sc <- spark_connect(method = "databricks_connect")
tbl(sc, I("samples.nyctaxi.trips"))
#> Error in UseMethod("sql_render") : 
#>  no applicable method for 'sql_render' applied to an object of class "c('src_spark_connection', 'src_oldClass', 'src_dbi', 'src_sql', 'src')"
```

Any operation after connecting fails with:

```
Error in UseMethod():
! no applicable method for 'invoke' applied to an object of class
  "c('spark_connection', 'DBIConnection')"
```

The issue is in `R/dplyr.R`. Several functions retrieve the connection from a
`tbl_pyspark` via direct positional subscript (`x[[1]]`):

```r
# spark_dataframe.tbl_pyspark
conn <- x[[1]]

# tbl_pyspark_sdf
con <- python_conn(x[[1]])

# python_obj_tbl_set
tbl[[1]] <- sc
```

In sparklyr 1.9.5 (PR sparklyr/sparklyr#3518), the tbl `src` slot was restructured
for dbplyr 2.6.0 compatibility. `x[[1]]` no longer returns the full
`connect_databricks`/`pyspark_connection` object — it returns a stripped
`c('spark_connection', 'DBIConnection')` with no `invoke` method.

Two fixes needed:

1. Define `spark_connection.tbl_pyspark` so `spark_connection(tbl)` doesn't fall
   through to sparklyr's implementation (which calls `dbplyr::remote_con()` and
   returns the wrong class):
   ```r
   #' @export
   spark_connection.tbl_pyspark <- function(x, ...) {
     x[["src"]]
   }
   ```
2. Replace `x[[1]]` with `spark_connection(x)` in `spark_dataframe.tbl_pyspark`,
   `tbl_pyspark_sdf`, and `python_obj_tbl_set`.

Reported here: https://github.com/mlverse/pysparklyr/pull/184#issuecomment-4774099559

title: databricks_connect pins the SDK auth_type, which breaks Databricks Workload Identity (file-oidc)
description:
### Description

When `spark_connect(method = "databricks_connect")` runs in an environment configured for Databricks workload identity federation (e.g. Posit Connect with Databricks workload identity OAuth integration), the connection fails to authenticate even though the Databricks SDK capable of handling this.

### Cause

In `databricks_sdk_client()` (connect-databricks-utils.R), auth_type is forced based only on whether a static token string is present:

```
if (token == "") {
  databricks_desktop_login(host = host, profile = profile)
  auth_type <- "databricks-cli"
} else {
  auth_type <- "pat"
}
config <- sdk$core$Config(host = host, token = token, auth_type = auth_type, ...)
```

Workload identity doesn't have a static token (`token == ""`), so `auth_type` is pinned to `"databricks-cli"`. Explicitly setting `auth_type` overrides the SDK's own auth resolution, so the file-oidc/env-oidc strategy never runs — despite `DATABRICKS_AUTH_TYPE`, `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID`, and `DATABRICKS_OIDC_TOKEN_FILEPATH` all being set in the environment. Instead the connection then attempts (and fails) Databricks CLI auth.

### Related

The same workload identity setup works out of the box with `odbc::databricks()` and the Databricks Python SDK/SQL connector, but not via `databricks_connect`, because those let the SDK resolve auth_type itself.

### Suggested fix

When no explicit token/profile is provided, don't override `auth_type` — let the SDK resolve it (e.g. construct `Config()` without forcing `auth_type`, or only force it when a PAT/CLI path is actually intended). The method already builds `sdk_config <- db_sdk$core$Config()` earlier to pull the token; that config has the correct auth strategy resolved and could be reused.

### Environment
pysparklyr 0.1.9 (also present on main / 0.2.1)

title: `spark_connect()` ignores named `~/.databrickscfg` profile for token when `master` is passed explicitly
description:
When using `spark_connect(method = "databricks_connect")` with an explicit `master` parameter and a named `~/.databrickscfg` profile, the token is resolved from `[DEFAULT]` instead of the named profile. This causes HTTP 403 errors when the `[DEFAULT]` profile points to a different workspace than the one specified in `master`.

## Scenario

Our organization (IU Health) runs **separate Azure Databricks workspaces per project** . Each workspace has its own host URL and token. Our `~/.databrickscfg` looks like:

```ini
[DEFAULT]
host = https://adb-AAAA.azuredatabricks.net
token = dapi_workspace_A...

[patvolume]
host = https://adb-BBBB.azuredatabricks.net
token = dapi_workspace_B...
```

## Reproducer

```r
library(sparklyr)
library(pysparklyr)

# This FAILS with HTTP 403 — token comes from [DEFAULT], not [patvolume]
sc <- spark_connect(
  method = "databricks_connect",
  master = "https://adb-BBBB.azuredatabricks.net",
  cluster_id = "xxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxxxxx"
)
```

**Expected:** Token is resolved from the `[patvolume]` profile (matching the host) or from a `profile` parameter.

**Actual:** `databricks_token()` returns the `[DEFAULT]` token → HTTP 403 Forbidden because that token is for workspace A, not workspace B.

## Root Cause

In `R/connect-databricks-utils.R`, `databricks_token()` checks these sources in order:

1. Explicit `token` argument
2. `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` env var
3. `CONNECT_DATABRICKS_TOKEN` env var
4. Posit Workbench config
5. **Fallback:** `db_sdk$core$Config()` — no arguments, reads `[DEFAULT]` only

The `profile` parameter from `spark_connect()` is never passed to `databricks_token()`. By the time the profile is consulted (in `databricks_sdk_client()`), the token has already been resolved from the wrong source.

In contrast, Python's `DatabricksSession.builder.profile("patvolume").getOrCreate()` works correctly because it reads both host and token from the named profile in a single operation.

## Workaround

Parse `~/.databrickscfg` manually in R and pass the token explicitly:

```r
# Read token from named profile
cfg <- readLines("~/.databrickscfg", warn = FALSE)
in_profile <- FALSE
token <- ""
for (line in cfg) {
  if (grepl("^\\[patvolume\\]", line)) { in_profile <- TRUE; next }
  if (grepl("^\\[", line)) { in_profile <- FALSE; next }
  if (in_profile && grepl("^\\s*token\\s*=", line)) {
    token <- trimws(sub("^\\s*token\\s*=\\s*", "", line))
  }
}

# Pass token explicitly — this works
sc <- spark_connect(
  method = "databricks_connect",
  master = "https://adb-BBBB.azuredatabricks.net",
  cluster_id = "xxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxxxxx",
  token = token
)
```

## Suggested Fix

Thread the `profile` parameter into `databricks_token()` so the fallback path uses it:

```r
# In databricks_token(), change the fallback from:
sdk_config <- db_sdk$core$Config()

# To:
sdk_config <- db_sdk$core$Config(profile = profile)
```

This would make the Python SDK read the correct named profile for token resolution, consistent with how `DatabricksSession.builder.profile()` works on the Python side.

## Environment

- sparklyr 1.8.6 / pysparklyr (latest as of Feb 2026)
- databricks-connect 16.4.x
- R 4.4.x via Nix
- Azure Databricks (multiple workspaces)
- DBR 16.4.x-scala2.12

## Impact

This affects any organization using multiple Databricks workspaces with named `~/.databrickscfg` profiles — an increasingly common pattern in healthcare and enterprise environments with data isolation requirements. The workaround is functional but fragile and requires users to understand the internal token resolution order.

## Related

- pysparklyr #88: Support for databrickscfg file (closed, Dec 2023) — addressed `[DEFAULT]` reading but not named profiles
- Databricks docs: [Unified authentication](https://docs.databricks.com/en/dev-tools/auth.html#databricks-client-unified-authentication)
- Python SDK `DatabricksSession.builder.profile("name")` handles this correctly — pysparklyr's R-side token resolution should match that behavior

title: Add support for new ML methodology
description:
Spark 4.0 added support for `pyspark.ml` in Connect. This expands the available ML functions, but the wrappers need to be written for the other models, as well as to update the existing ones.

Here is an example script showing the steps to fit a Linear Regression model: 

```r
library(sparklyr)

pysparklyr::spark_connect_service_start("4.0", "2.13")
#> Starting Spark Connect locally ...
#>   starting org.apache.spark.sql.connect.service.SparkConnectServer, logging to
#>   /Users/edgar/spark/spark-4.0.0-bin-hadoop3/logs/spark-edgar-org.apache.spark.sql.connect.service.SparkConnectServer-1-edgarruiz-WL57.out

Sys.sleep(1)
sc <- spark_connect(
  master = "sc://localhost",
  method = "spark_connect",
  version = "4.0"
)
#> ℹ Attempting to load 'r-sparklyr-pyspark-4.0'
#> ✔ Python environment: 'r-sparklyr-pyspark-4.0' [410ms]
#> 

tbl_mtcars <- copy_to(sc, mtcars, overwrite = TRUE)

# New ML methodology 
ps <- reticulate::import("pyspark")
va <- ps$ml$feature$VectorAssembler()
as <- va$copy()
as$setInputCols(c("wt", "am", "vs"))
#> VectorAssembler_4c696c095e90
as$setOutputCol("features")
#> VectorAssembler_4c696c095e90
sdf_prep <- spark_dataframe(tbl_mtcars)
```

title: Fails to connect when rendering RMarkdown or Quarto in Workbench
description:
Authentication fails when rendering an RMarkdown document. This is specific to using the OAuth integration with Workbench and Databricks. 
The root cause is that RStudio's `.rs.api.getDatabricksToken()` is available during interactive sessions, but not when rendering a document. The more likely way to solve is by reading the configuration file directly. `odbc` does that here: https://github.com/r-dbi/odbc/blob/d9f220d0a6b186fe9d71f9de302c7b4cd6936fdd/R/driver-databricks.R#L328-L343.

title: Unset the `RETICULATE_PYTHON` variable if one is set
description:
Due to the complex Python version handling required to properly connect to a Spark/Databricks Connect instance, the default environment provided in `RETICULATE_PYTHON` will work. Maybe in very few cases it may work, but for the vast majority of cases  we will need a custom Python env.  If set, `reticulate` will prevent `sparklyr` from selecting a different environment.

The idea is to have the functions that serve as entry points, namely `spark_connect()`, and `install_databricks()`/ `install_pyspark()`, to unset `RETICULATE_PYTHON`  when they first run, so that they can create and interact with the correct Python environment.  As an escape-hatch,  this new behavior can be disabled via a new argument that we'll add to those entry point functions.

title: `reticulate can only bind to copies of Python built with '--enable-shared'.`
description:
Adding this reference here to help users with debugging.

Error message:

```r
.....reticulate can only bind to copies of Python built with '--enable-shared'.
```

This is happening because there is no Python installation that `reticulate` can use. `pysparklyr` depends on that package to function.

The best way to resolve is to run:

```r
reticulate::install_python()
```

If the output mentions `--skip-existing [version number]` then you will have two options:

- If you're ok with replacing the existing Python, then use:
```r
reticulate::install_python(version = "[version number]", force = TRUE)
```

- If you would like to keep that installation of Python then use a different version number:
```r
reticulate::install_python(version = "[slightly version number]")
``` 
For example, if the version number is `3.9.12`, then use `3.9.18`: 

```r
reticulate::install_python(version = "3.9.18")
```

title: Use arrow package to move data to/from pyspark?
description:
Thinking along the lines of https://arrow.apache.org/blog/2019/01/25/r-spark-improvements/, there could be some perf gains to use Arrow to move the data rather than going through pandas. Arrow also supports ALTREP now. Using arrow could also help prevent lossy type conversions.

Like with sparklyr, you could put `arrow` in Suggests so that you don't require it. Or you could use https://github.com/apache/arrow-nanoarrow, which is a much lighter dependency.

Figure out a process to avoid overwhelming the RStudio Connections Pane when the number of tables is so high that it overwhelms the pane, and causes the RStudio session to crash.  

The most obvious approach is to limit the number of tables to display to 1,000, and add an `option` to customize that limit. But there may be a better way to handle this.

title: Avoid installing `pyspark` when installing `databricks-connect`
description:
To use DB Connect sessions, the Python environment should avoid installing `pyspark` directly, reference found here: https://docs.databricks.com/en/dev-tools/databricks-connect-ref.html#conflicting-pyspark-installations

On the surface, the best way to do this, would be to have separate convenience functions to install `pyspark`, but not `databricks-connect`, and the other way around. I am leaning towards using the current `install_pyspark()` to install `pyspark`, and a new `install_databricks()` for the other.  

An additional request, is to add support for versions. This would give the end-user the ability to install previous versions of the main Python libraries. The main challenge, is that the dependencies (as in the other Python libraries, such as the gRCP library) will need to match. So we need to find a good, safe way to do this. The current thought, is to use the public Posit Package Manager's snapshots ability, and tie `pyspark` and `databricks.connect` versions to snapshot dates, so that all the dependency versions match properly (https://packagemanager.posit.co/client/#/repos/pypi/setup?snapshot=2023-08-01)

title: PySpark 3.4.1 - `copy_to()` not working
description:
```r
pysparklyr::spark_connect_service_start()
devtools::load_all()
library(sparklyr)

sc <- spark_connect(
  master = "sc://localhost",
  method = "spark_connect"
)

copy_to(sc, mtcars)
```
The previous code, returns the following error: 

```r
Error in py_call_impl(callable, call_args$unnamed, call_args$named) : 
  pyspark.errors.exceptions.connect.SparkConnectGrpcException: (java.util.NoSuchElementException) spark.sql.session.localRelationCacheThreshold
Run `reticulate::py_last_error()` for details.
```

The resolution is to add a default, if none is set:

```r
sc$python_obj$conf$set("spark.sql.session.localRelationCacheThreshold", 1048576L)
```

The default number is to match what it's in the tests within Spark:  https://github.com/apache/spark/blob/ce6b5f3751e9ea5d1cb4b63c8e14235914817766/python/pyspark/sql/tests/connect/test_connect_basic.py#L668-L671
